pr_title: Fix hitobjects potentially ending up outside playfield when selection is scaled
pr_body:
(Sort of) Fixes https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/11202

**Issues:**
 - When a selection is scaled  it can end up wider/higher than the playfield, pushing hitobjects outside the playfield.
 - Hitobjects can be scaled beyond the right/bottom border regardless of selection size
 - The selection box can move around in unexpected ways when sliders are involved.(Not really addressed in this PR, but the user can no longer push objects outside the playfield)
 


**Solution:**
 - Make sure selection does not end up larger than the playfield.
 - Ensure objects are moved back in bounds while scaling
<details>

Before:
![before](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22643729/108611467-03961200-73df-11eb-81ca-b9f67c474e10.gif)

After:
![after](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22643729/108611470-07299900-73df-11eb-9254-81f49b05b7fe.gif)
 
</details>

**Remarks:**
- Selections with multiple sliders involved still behave in unexpected ways, which is why I am not sure if https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/11202 should be closed by this PR or not
- Another option would be to stop scaling the selection altogether once the user tries to drag it past the border instead of scaling it in the opposite direction. I can try implementing it that way if you would prefer it.
pr_comments:
> Another option would be to stop scaling the selection altogether once the user tries to drag it past the border instead of scaling it in the opposite direction. I can try implementing it that way if you would prefer it.

I think that's way more intuitive. Having a left drag handle make the selection wider from the right side seems plain weird.

I changed the scaling bounds logic to hopefully behave more intuitively. Slider scaling still feels kind of bad, but I don't think it's any worse than the current master behavior.

<details>

![New Behavior](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22643729/108633522-e6138780-7474-11eb-9f70-1e419cac3ade.gif)

</details>

There are some edge cases that seem to not be working too well ([see video](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1O2iOm-uruyMXqpi7FUVIDwHzV6Xj_x8u/view?usp=sharing)).

Same thing happens for "non-zero-width" selections, if an object is on the right or bottom edge of the playfield.
@FamousPig are you planning on looking into the remaining issues with this PR? no pressure, just checking in.
Sorry about the long silence. I have an idea for how to solve the remaining issues but it comes with it's own problems. I am planning to take another look hopefully this weekend.

Again apologies for the long delay. 

For multi-object scaling, I have made changes to clamp the scale to the playfield-size and close to 0 instead of outright aborting it. This should avoid the problem of scale getting stuck in weird ways or moving around(as long as no sliders are involved). 

For single-slider scaling I have not really found a great solution. Since the behavior of the calculated sliderpath while scaling the control points is hard to predict, I don't see a better option than "try it, if it doesn't work revert it". This can lead to unintuitive behavior near the edge where scaling in any direction is impossible.

issue_context.title: The selection box can drag objects outside the playfield when resized
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug:** 
- edit a beatmap
- select some objects
- resizing the selection doesn't clamp to the playfield size

and it's not just a visual issue: if you save the beatmap, the objects are in that location.


**Screenshots or videos showing encountered issue:**
![editor](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/43073074/102612559-34cd3a00-4131-11eb-84cd-dc92152192ef.gif)
![gameplay](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/43073074/102612678-74942180-4131-11eb-8e4b-c29820ad6f8e.png)

**osu!lazer version:** 2020.1212.0

review_comments:
Was there any reason not to use `getClampedScale()` (or at least that zero-or-negative-scale part) here? Because it isn't used, individual sliders can still be "flipped" or resized past the playfield size.

That's about the only remaining issue I have managed to find after some fiddling, though. Looks solid to me otherwise :+1:

When you say "resize past the playfield size", you are talking about the slider body, correct? I wasn't really concerned with keeping the body in the playfield since it isn't respected by movement either in stable or lazer. I figured that was the intended behavior.

`getClampedScale()` won't work directly in this case, since the method of scaling is to different from multi-object scaling. The original plan was to create some kind of overload for use in `scaleSlider()` before I figured out that limiting the max scale (as in finding the closest possible scale where sliderhead and sliderend stay in bounds) isn't feasible here.

I limited the minimum size for single slider scaling.
